notes.title: Patch Update .8.3
notes.content:
Louie version .8.3 is live! Thank you, everyone, for all your bug reports and feedback so far. 

Here is what's new.

There are two big changes.
[list]
[*] Louie's wall collisions are more forgiving now. It used to be that if you pushed against a wall and jumped, you wouldn't be able to jump high enough to clear the wall. Now, you can push against walls and jump, and you'll get the same height as if you weren't pushing against the wall.
[*] I changed the target frame rate and vSync settings in the game to prefer vSync over frame rate. This change is subtle, but should help reduce screen tearing, and should help prevent unnecessary GPU load. I learned that without vSync, the Unity game engine will crank out as many frames as it can between each monitor refresh, even if it doesn't need to do so to produce a smooth frame rate. The GPU was being seriously overworked for no good reason. I need to do further testing and research to figure out how important this was in overall GPU heat and load, but I'm fairly confident this is a step in the right direction. 
For benchmarking, I put Louie in a big area in the level, Kiddie Cone, and measured GPU temperature on a macbook pro, and on a desktop equipped with a gtx1080. In the previous version (.8.2), the temperature on the laptop was in the 90's (scary). In the new version (.8.3), the temperature was in the 70's. Thats a pretty solid difference. I didn't notice a big difference on the gtx1080 card, but, its also a much beefier card to begin with.
[/list]


And here are the rest of the changes.
[list]
[*] The editor no longer accumulates semi-transparent copies of props as you make a level
[*] The z-index ordering on the controller "use" hint is fixed
[*] The editor has slightly better iconography. Various prop categories, and a few objects had incorrect icons. 
[*] The editor prop selection screen fits on the screen better
[*] Fixed a typo in the final level of the game
[*] Fixed a pause-screen & controller related bug where pushing "B" caused the pause screen to flicker on/off
[/list]

Thanks for taking the time to read this patch update! 
If you have further bug reports, let me know in the Steam Discussion pages.

-Chris

notes.title: Louie is available now!
notes.content:
The game is done! Its ready! You can play it right now!
I'm thrilled to announce that after 2 years of development, Louie is available on Steam. 

Get ready to track down all that stolen ice cream the evil Dr. Melt has stolen and hidden away on the island. There are 26 levels to beat, a full level editor, a bajillion secrets to find, and a bunch of hats to collect. 

Thank you to everyone who wish-listed the game and helped support me during development. I couldn't have done it with you.

notes.title: Summer Ice Cream Theft
notes.content:
Gather one and all, and behold a tale of dastardly malice. The once respected Dr. Melt has turned evil, and has stolen the world Ice Cream supply just ahead of the heat of summer! Your mission, if you choose to accept it, is to storm the remote island base of Dr. Melt, and recover as much Ice Cream as possible. You'll play as Agent Louie, a talented super spy.

Mysteriously, Dr. Melt's defenses look shockingly similar to some fictitious games of the past. The game, [i]Secret Agent (1992)[/i], had players controlling a secret spy through the Diabolical Villain Society (D.V.S.). Its as if the spirit of the D.V.S. lives on in Dr. Melt's compounds. Lasers, lava, henchmen, robots, and hidden keys stand in the way of finding all the Ice Cream. However, Dr. Melt has taken a shine towards hidden passage ways and secret rooms. Dr. Melt's evil base is crammed full of secret content to uncover. 

I've been working on [i]Louie[/i] since November 2018, and I'm on track to release the full game this September. You can look at some old development checkpoints on my [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-EWJEAeTgqk]Youtube channel[/url]. I've always loved making games, and [i]Louie[i] will be my first publicly available game, ever. I've built the game for myself, but I know you, too, can enjoy it.

notes.title: 0.5.7 Released
notes.content:
I'm pleased to announce that Louie 0.5.7 has been released! The two biggest call outs in this release are definitely the addition floor push-buttons, and all the game progression tracking. Levels now keep track of your best scores, and how many secrets and pickups you have left to find. This release also marks the end of feature development for Louie. At this point, the remaining work falls neatly into bug fixing, level design, and steam achievements.

[list]
[*] subtle visual improvement to dbl jump
[*] boxes should really now not kill you if they're on lava
[*] editor includes floor push buttons
[*] new level, "Lemon Squeezy" that has push buttons
[*] cheat codes can be used through the in-game console (if you want to know them, ask, or guess)
[*] current secret/pickup scores can be seen on pause screen
[*] score screen includes a x/5 grading mechanism, where the score is derived from your health, pickups, and secrets found.
[*] total secrets/pickups, best score are recorded per level and shown on the island map
[*] score screen has a continue button hint.
[*] island level selection has a play button hint
[*] security cameras can be shot
[*] moving platforms can have a color field
[/list]

(when you look at a level from the island-map, you can see your best score)
